definition_zh: v. 校准，标定（仪器）；精确测量；（仔细地）调整
definition_en: to check or adjust an instrument against a known standard; to measure something precisely
core_image: 一枚标准砝码放在秤盘上，指针被调回零
scene: 仪器出厂前要用标准砝码一件件校准。Each instrument is calibrated against a standard weight before it ships.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：calibrate 指用标准物校准仪器；句意是每件仪器出厂前都要用标准砝码校准。

senses.title: To adjust against a standard
senses.definition: to compare a measuring device with a known value and correct its readings
senses.definitionCN: 把测量装置与已知数值比较，并修正其读数
senses.example: The lab calibrates its scales every Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室每周一校准天平。
senses.why: The word comes from the bore of a gun, which was measured and matched to its shot.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自炮膛口径，原本要量准才能配上炮弹。

senses.title: To tune something finely
senses.definition: to set an action or judgement with great precision
senses.definitionCN: 以极高精度设定某个动作或判断
senses.example: Her responses were calibrated to the mood of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回应与房间里的气氛精准配合。
senses.why: From instruments the word moves to human behaviour that is measured and adjusted.
senses.whyCN: 从仪器延伸到被衡量和调整的人的行为。

intro.en: Calibrate comes from calibre, the measured bore of a gun.
intro.cn: calibrate 源自 calibre，即量好的炮膛内径。

items.en: Qalib means a mould for casting.
items.cn: qalib 意为铸造用的模子。

items.en: Calibre means the bore of a gun.
items.cn: calibre 意为炮膛内径。

items.en: To calibrate means to measure the bore.
items.cn: 十九世纪动词意为测量口径。

items.en: Instruments are calibrated against standards.

items.en: Mass production demands routine calibration.

normalIntro.en: Calibrate is to make the gauge agree with the truth.
normalIntro.cn: calibrate 就是让刻度与事实对上。

normal.en: Calibre is a measured bore.
To calibrate is to measure it.

People can be calibrated too.
normal.cn: 人的反应也可以被调准。

abstract.en: A needle brought back to zero.
abstract.cn: 被拨回零点的指针。

abstract.en: Two measures agreeing on one weight.
abstract.cn: 两种量法在一个重量上达成一致。

abstract.en: Trust built by a standard lump of metal.
abstract.cn: 靠一块标准金属建立起来的信任。

examples.en: Engineers calibrated the sensor before the test.
examples.cn: 工程师在测试前校准了传感器。

examples.en: The dial needs calibrating every six months.
examples.cn: 这个表盘每半年需要校准。

examples.en: Her tone was calibrated to sound friendly.
examples.cn: 她的语气被调得听起来很友好。

root: calibre（口径）+ -ate（动词后缀）→ 量准口径；校准

definition_zh: n. 才干，水准；（枪炮的）口径；（管子的）内径
definition_en: the quality of a person or work; the internal width of a gun barrel or tube
core_image: 枪管里那道被量得极准的圆
scene: 枪管的口径决定了能装进多大的弹。The calibre of the barrel decides which bullets fit.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：calibre 指口径；句意是枪管的口径决定了能装进什么样的子弹。

senses.title: Quality of mind or work
senses.definition: the level of ability or quality that a person or thing shows
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物表现出的能力或品质水平
senses.example: We need someone of her calibre for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 这个职位需要她这种水准的人。
senses.why: The measured bore became a metaphor for measured ability.
senses.whyCN: 量准的口径被用作衡量能力的比喻。

senses.title: The width of a barrel
senses.definition: the inside diameter of a gun barrel or a tube
senses.definitionCN: 枪管或管子的内径
senses.example: The rifle fires a small calibre round.
senses.exampleCN: 这支步枪发射小口径子弹。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from the mould used to cast shot.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，源自铸弹用的模子。

intro.en: Calibre comes from an Arabic word for a mould, which fixed the size of what was cast.

items.en: Qalib means a mould.

items.en: Writers speak of a man of calibre.
items.cn: 十八世纪出现「有分量的人」的说法。

items.en: Tubes and wires are graded by calibre.
items.cn: 十九世纪管材线材按口径分级。

items.en: Calibre means both bore and ability.
items.cn: 现代兼指口径与才干。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cal- opening; the near-meaning group puts quality words first and measuring words second.

entries.definition: To adjust against a standard.

A tool for measuring diameter.
How good something is.
The value a person has earned.

The width across a round shape.

normalIntro.en: Calibre is the size of the hole and the size of the person.

normal.en: A mould sets the size of a shot.
The barrel must match it.
That width is the calibre.
People also have a calibre.
Same word, measured worth.

abstract.en: A circle measured to the millimetre.
abstract.cn: 精确到毫米的一个圆。

abstract.en: The width that decides what fits.
abstract.cn: 决定什么能放进去的宽度。

abstract.en: Ability spoken of as a bore.
abstract.cn: 被当作膛径来谈论的能力。

examples.en: The journal publishes work of the highest calibre.
examples.cn: 这家期刊发表最高水准的研究。

examples.en: The pistol is of a smaller calibre than the rifle.
examples.cn: 这把枪的口径比步枪小。

examples.en: She is a lawyer of real calibre.
examples.cn: 她是一位真正有分量的律师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开利伯」——先量准口径，才谈得上水平。

root: 阿拉伯 qalib（模子）→ 法语 calibre（口径）→ 才干、水准

sensesIntro.en: The bore and the person are both measured: one by a gauge, the other by the work produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 膛径与人都在被衡量：一个用量规，一个看作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a precisely measured circle inside a barrel
core.cn: 核心意象：枪管内部被量得极准的一个圆

branches.cn: 撑起一本期刊的水准之作。

intro.cn: calibre 是 calibrate 的来源名词；下面列出其词尾以及「测量」词场的词缀。

definition_zh: 平静的；镇定的；使平静；平静
definition_en: not worried, angry or excited
core_image: 无风时平整如镜的海面
scene: 暴风雨刚过，海面重新变得平滑。The sea grew calm after the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 calm 是「平静的」（第 1 个义项：没有风浪、水面平稳）；句意是暴风雨后海面平静下来。

derivatives.zh: 使风平浪静，使停住不动

senses.title: Still, without wind or waves
senses.definition: of water or weather, still and without strong movement
senses.definitionCN: 水面或天气静止、没有强烈活动
senses.example: The sea grew calm after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后海面平静下来。
senses.why: The core image is a sea flattened to a mirror after wind drops.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是风停后海面平得像一面镜子。

senses.title: Not excited or upset
senses.definition: of a person, not worried, angry or excited
senses.definitionCN: 人没有忧虑、怒气或激动
senses.example: She stayed calm while the others shouted.
senses.exampleCN: 别人大喊时她保持镇定。
senses.why: A quiet mind is pictured as a still sea.
senses.whyCN: 安静的心被比作平静的海面。

senses.title: To make someone quiet
senses.definition: to make a person or situation quiet and steady
senses.definitionCN: 使人或局面安静稳定下来
senses.example: He calmed the crying child.
senses.exampleCN: 他哄住了哭泣的孩子。
senses.why: The adjective became a verb meaning to bring about that still state.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为动词，指带来那种平静的状态。

intro.en: Calm came through French from a Latin word for midday heat.
intro.cn: calm 经法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语里表示正午炎热的词。

items.en: kauma meant burning heat.
items.cn: 希腊语 kauma 意为灼热。

items.en: cauma named the heat of midday, when work stops.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cauma 指正午炎热、停工休息的时段。

items.en: calme named a time of rest and quiet.
items.cn: 古法语 calme 指休息与安静的时刻。

items.en: calm described still air and still water.
items.cn: 中古英语 calm 形容静止的空气与水面。

items.en: Calm covers weather, mood and the act of soothing.
items.cn: 现代英语中 calm 兼指天气、情绪与安抚的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the calm base; the near-meaning group gives other quiet words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 calm 词基；近义组是其他表示安静的词。

the state of being calm
to leave a ship without wind
quiet and free from trouble

normalIntro.en: Calm describes a still sea and a steady mind.

abstract.en: See a hand rest gently on a shaking shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻按在发抖的肩上。

examples.en: The sea grew calm after the storm.

examples.en: He calmed the crying child.
examples.cn: 他哄住了哭泣的孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: calm 读起来像「卡姆」，一口气卡住不出声，四周立刻安静下来，正是 calm 的平静。

sensesIntro.en: A still sea, a steady mind, and the act of soothing.
sensesIntro.cn: 平静的海面、稳定的心，以及安抚的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sea flattened to a mirror.

definition_zh: n. 卡路里，卡（食物热量单位）；卡（热量单位）
definition_en: a unit for measuring the energy in food; also a small unit of heat in physics
core_image: 食品包装背面那一行小小的数字
scene: 包装背面列着每一百克含多少卡路里。The label lists how many calories each bar contains.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：calorie 指食物热量单位；句意是包装列出每根含多少卡路里。

senses.title: The food energy unit
senses.definition: the unit used on food labels, equal to a thousand small calories
senses.definitionCN: 食品标签所用单位，等于一千小卡
senses.example: A slice of bread has about seventy calories.
senses.exampleCN: 一片面包约含七十卡路里。
senses.why: The word began as a heat unit and was later applied to food.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是热量单位，后来才用于食物。

senses.title: The small heat unit
senses.definition: the amount of heat needed to raise one gram of water by one degree
senses.definitionCN: 使一克水升温摄氏一度所需的热量
senses.example: Physicists still use the small calorie in calculations.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家计算时仍使用小卡。
senses.why: The scientific sense is older and remains in physics.
senses.whyCN: 科学义更古老，并保留在物理学中。

definition_zh: n. 诽谤，诬蔑；诽谤性的言论

scene: 一封匿名信把他说成骗子，没人去查证。The calumny spread faster than any correction could.

definition_zh: 伪装；使动物、装备或人不易被发现的体色、形态或掩饰手段
definition_en: the colors, shapes or devices that make an animal, person or object hard to see or detect
core_image: 一只蛾的翅纹与树皮纹理完全重合，停上去就消失不见
scene: 树干上的蛾子把翅膀张开，翅面的斑纹与地衣的碎块几乎重合，寻找它的鸟从旁边飞过。The moth spreads its wings against the trunk until the patches match the lichen, and the bird hunting it passes by, a textbook example of camouflage.
sceneCN: 这里 camouflage 指「使动物不易被发现的体色与斑纹」（第 1 个义项：外形与背景融为一体）；句意为蛾子的翅纹与地衣几乎重合，捕食的鸟从旁边飞过也没发现它。图中可辨识物件：树干、地衣、展开翅膀的蛾、飞过的鸟。

pos.zh: 伪装；保护色；掩饰手段（不可数）

senses.title: Animal protective coloration
senses.definition: the colors and patterns that let an animal blend into its background
senses.definitionCN: 使动物与背景融为一体、难以被看见的颜色与图案
senses.example: The moth's wing patches match the lichen exactly.
senses.exampleCN: 蛾翅上的斑块与地衣完全相合。
senses.why: the word first served hunters and naturalists describing animals that seem to vanish against bark, sand or leaves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初服务于猎人与博物学者，用来描述在树皮、沙地或叶片前仿佛消失的动物。

senses.title: Concealment by behavior
senses.definition: actions such as freezing, crouching or changing posture that reduce visibility
senses.definitionCN: 静止、伏低或改变姿态等降低可见度的动作
senses.example: The fawn lies flat and does not move while the doe feeds.
senses.exampleCN: 母鹿觅食时，幼鹿趴平不动。
senses.why: camouflage is not only worn; it is also done, and stillness can hide an animal whose colors already match.
senses.whyCN: 伪装不只穿在身上，也做在动作里；静止能藏住一只颜色已相配的动物。

senses.title: Military camouflage
senses.definition: the disguising of troops, vehicles and positions to avoid detection
senses.definitionCN: 使部队、车辆与阵地不被发现而进行的掩饰
senses.example: The battery was hidden under camouflage netting.
senses.exampleCN: 炮兵连被伪装网遮住。
senses.why: modern warfare made the word famous: a gun that can be seen is a gun that will be hit.
senses.whyCN: 现代战争让这个词广为人知：能被看见的火炮，就是会被击中的火炮。

senses.title: Camouflage clothing and material
senses.definition: the printed fabrics, nets and covers used to hide people or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 用于隐藏人员或装备的印花布料、网与遮盖物
senses.example: The unit wore woodland camouflage in the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队在森林里穿林地迷彩。
senses.why: metonymy turns the method into the kit: the pattern itself comes to be called camouflage.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把方法变成装备：图案本身也被称作 camouflage。

senses.title: Figurative disguise of intent
senses.definition: words or actions that hide one's real purpose or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 掩盖真实目的或感受的言语与行动
senses.example: His calm tone was camouflage for panic.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的语气是对慌乱的掩饰。
senses.why: if a body can be hidden against a background, a motive can be hidden behind a manner.
senses.whyCN: 如果身体能藏在背景前，动机也能藏在举止后面。

senses.title: Protective coloration as a term
senses.definition: the biological term for coloration that lowers the chance of detection by predators or prey
senses.definitionCN: 指降低被天敌或猎物发现几率的体色的生物学术语
senses.example: Protective coloration is the scientific name for one kind of camouflage.
senses.exampleCN: 保护色是某一类伪装在科学上的名称。
senses.why: science needed a narrower label, so camouflage became the umbrella and protective coloration one branch under it.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要更窄的标签，于是 camouflage 成为伞名，保护色成为其下的一支。

senses.title: Resemblance to another object
senses.titleCN: 与另一物体相似的伪装形态
senses.definition: shapes that make an organism resemble a leaf, twig, stone or another species
senses.definitionCN: 使生物看起来像叶片、枝条、石头或另一物种的形态
senses.example: The insect's body mimics a dead twig.
senses.exampleCN: 这只昆虫的身体模仿一根枯枝。
senses.why: blending in and looking like something else are neighboring strategies, and everyday usage often puts both under camouflage.
senses.whyCN: 融入背景与长得像别的东西是相邻的策略，日常用法常把两者都归入 camouflage。

senses.title: Visual deception in design
senses.definition: the use of pattern and contrast to hide an object in plain sight, as in vehicles or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 用图案与对比把物体藏在显眼处，如车辆或建筑
senses.example: The aircraft's paint breaks up its outline against the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机的涂装打散了它在天空中的轮廓。
senses.why: the principle is general: high-contrast false edges defeat the eye that looks for a continuous outline.
senses.whyCN: 原理是通用的：高对比的假边缘能骗过寻找连续轮廓的眼睛。

intro.en: Camouflage came into English from French during the First World War; French camoufler 'to disguise' probably goes back to Italian camuffare, whose deeper origin is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: camouflage 在第一次世界大战期间由法语进入英语；法语 camoufler「伪装」大概可追溯到意大利语 camuffare，其更早来源不确定。年代为约数。

items.en: Camoufler meant 'to disguise, mask'; it was the verb used by French forces for hiding guns and positions from aerial observation.
items.cn: camoufler 意为「伪装、遮掩」；法国军队用它指把火炮与阵地隐藏起来，避开空中观察。

items.en: Italian camuffare 'to disguise, trick' is the likely source of the French verb; the two languages shared the term in military and theatrical circles.
items.cn: 意大利语 camuffare「伪装、欺骗」是法语动词的可能来源；两种语言在军事与戏剧圈中共用这个词。

items.en: Source uncertain: camuffare may involve capo 'head' plus muffare 'to muffle', but this is a suggestion, not an established derivation, and no reliable Latin root can be asserted.
items.cn: 来源不确定：camuffare 可能由 capo「头」与 muffare「包裹、闷住」组成，但这只是推测，并非确立的派生；无法断言可靠的拉丁词根。

items.en: English adopted camouflage during the First World War, first for the disguising of artillery and later for the painted patterns themselves.
items.cn: 英语在第一次世界大战期间借入 camouflage，最初指火炮的掩饰，后来指涂装图案本身。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to animal coloration, hunting gear, fashion and figurative disguise of intention.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到动物体色、狩猎装备、时装，以及比喻性的意图掩饰。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on camouflage itself; group two holds neighboring strategies of concealment and imitation.
note.cn: 第一组是 camouflage 本身构成的形式；第二组是相邻的隐蔽与模仿策略。

entries.definition: Hidden by camouflage; the -ed form describes the object, while camouflage names the method or material.
entries.definitionCN: 被伪装遮住的；-ed 形式描述对象，而 camouflage 命名方法或材料。

entries.definition: A person who designs or applies camouflage, especially in the military; the French agent noun is rare in English.
entries.definitionCN: 设计或实施伪装的人，尤指军中；这个法语施动名词在英语中罕用。

entries.definition: A net printed or scrimmed to hide equipment; the compound narrows camouflage to one piece of kit.
entries.definitionCN: 用于遮盖装备的印花或网眼织物；该复合词把 camouflage 收窄为一件装备。

entries.definition: The informal short form for camouflage pattern or clothing; it has lost the final syllables and most of the formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 伪装图案或服装的口语简称；省去末尾音节，也去掉了大部分正式语气。

entries.definition: The evolved resemblance of one organism to another; camouflage hides an animal in its background, mimicry makes it look like something else.
entries.definitionCN: 一种生物与另一种生物的演化相似；camouflage 把动物藏进背景，mimicry 让它看起来像别的东西。

entries.definition: A change of appearance meant to deceive; camouflage is one means of disguise, especially in the visual field.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗而改变外观；camouflage 是伪装的一种手段，尤在视觉层面。

entries.definition: The act of keeping something out of sight; it is the general purpose that camouflage serves.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物藏在视线之外的行为；是 camouflage 所服务的一般目的。

entries.definition: Coloration that reduces detection; it is the scientific term for one kind of camouflage.
entries.definitionCN: 降低被发现几率的体色；是某一类伪装在科学上的名称。

normal.en: The word is French military vocabulary adopted in 1917: first the act of masking guns, then the painted pattern.

normal.en: The family runs camouflage, camouflaged, camouflaging, camoufleur and the clipping camo.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 camouflage、camouflaged、camouflaging、camoufleur 与缩略 camo。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one trick: match the background, then hold still, then hide troops, wear the pattern, mask a motive, name the biological branch, resemble another object, and deceive the eye in design.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an outline that stops being an outline because the surface behind it is repeated on it.

branches.en: THE BIOLOGY: matching the background, naming the branch, and resembling another object are three related tricks.
branches.cn: 生物学：与背景相合、命名分支、像另一物体，是三个相关把戏。

branches.en: STILLNESS: behavior completes what coloration begins.
branches.cn: 静止：行为补全体色开始的事。

branches.en: THE MILITARY: the word's modern fame comes from hiding guns and then wearing the pattern.
branches.cn: 军事：这个词的现代名声来自藏炮，随后是穿上图案。

branches.en: HIDDEN MOTIVE: words and actions disguise what is really intended.
branches.cn: 隐藏的动机：言语与行动掩盖真实意图。

branches.en: DESIGN: false edges defeat the eye that searches for a continuous outline.
branches.cn: 设计：假边缘骗过寻找连续轮廓的眼睛。

intro.en: Camouflage is a French noun in -age built on the verb camoufler. English adds -ed, -ing and a clipping, but the deeper morphology is not reliably recoverable.

items.en: The root *ḱwṓn, dog, runs through the whole Indo-European dog-word family.
items.cn: 词根 *ḱwṓn（狗）贯穿整个印欧语系的「狗」词族。

items.en: Latin canarius meant of dogs, and Insulae Canariae, the Islands of the Dogs, was the Roman name for the archipelago.
items.cn: 拉丁语 canarius 意为「与狗有关的」，罗马人称该群岛为 Insulae Canariae（狗之群岛）。

items.en: Iberian sailors rendered the island name as Canaria and applied canario to the islands' small birds.
items.cn: 伊比利亚水手把岛名转写为 Canaria，并把 canario 用到群岛上的小型鸟类。

items.en: English canary bird first named the bird in the sixteenth century, later shortened to canary.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语先以 canary bird 称呼此鸟，后简化为 canary。

items.en: The yellow color sense appeared in the seventeenth century, applied to wine and cloth from the islands.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现黄色义，先用于群岛产的葡萄酒和布料。

items.en: The coal-mine warning practice gave the figurative sense, and American slang added the informer sense.
items.cn: 矿井预警的实践催生比喻义，美国俚语又添了告密者义。

note.en: Canary shares its dog root with a small word family and is easy to tangle with similarly spelled bird names.
note.cn: canary 的「狗」词根衍生出一小组词族，且容易与拼写相近的鸟类名混淆。

entries.definition: Of or like a dog, from the same Latin canis root.
entries.definitionCN: 犬的；犬齿，同出拉丁语 canis 词根。

entries.definition: A doghouse, from French chenil, ultimately the same dog root.
entries.definitionCN: 狗窝，经法语 chenil 上溯到同一「狗」词根。

entries.definition: A factory for canning food; only one letter from canary but from can.
entries.definitionCN: 罐头厂，与 canary 仅差一个字母，但源自 can（罐）。

entries.definition: A small open sandwich; spelled close but from a couch root.
entries.definitionCN: 小开胃点心，拼写相近但源自「沙发」一词根。

entries.definition: The bird family the canary belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 雀科，canary 所属的鸟类家族。

entries.definition: A guard or watcher that gives warning, the human figure of the canary role.
entries.definitionCN: 哨兵、守望者，是 canary 预警角色的人格化版本。

entries.definition: A leading indicator of trends, figurative like the mine canary.
entries.definitionCN: 领头羊、风向标，与矿井金丝雀同为比喻性指标。

entries.definition: One who betrays secrets, the plain word behind the slang sense.
entries.definitionCN: 告密者，是俚语义项背后的平实用词。

entries.definition: In political metaphor, the aggressive opposite of the small, warning songbird.
entries.definitionCN: 政治隐喻中的鹰派，与示警的小鸣禽形成象征性对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the island-of-dogs origin and the mine-shaft image.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「狗之群岛」词源与矿井画面的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Place first: Canary Islands, from Latin Insulae Canariae, the Islands of the Dogs.
normal.cn: 地名在先：加那利群岛源自拉丁语 Insulae Canariae（狗之群岛）。

normal.en: Same root: canary, canine, and kennel all descend from the dog word canis.
normal.cn: 同根记忆：canary、canine、kennel 都出自「狗」词 canis。

normal.en: Metaphor: a canary in a coal mine is the fixed phrase for an early-warning indicator.
normal.cn: 比喻义：固定说法「a canary in a coal mine」即「早期预警指标」。

normal.en: Color: canary yellow is the standard name for bright light yellow in fashion and design.
normal.cn: 颜色：canary yellow 是时尚与设计中明亮浅黄的标准色名。

normal.en: Slang hook: sing like a canary, to confess everything, links the bird's song to betrayal.
normal.cn: 俚语钩子：sing like a canary（全盘招供）把鸟鸣与告密连在一起。

abstract.en: A tiny yellow bird going quiet in the dark: everyone's alarm bell with feathers.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中一只突然噤声的小黄鸟：长着羽毛的警报器。

abstract.en: A swell of yellow paint across a gray wall, the room suddenly singing.
abstract.cn: 一抹淡黄刷过灰墙，整个房间顿时唱起歌来。

abstract.en: Dogs on a wild beach, named forever into an island, then into a bird.
abstract.cn: 野滩上的狗群：名字永远留给了岛，又从岛转给了鸟。

examples.en: Rising insurance claims were the canary that warned of the building's structural trouble.
examples.cn: 保险索赔的上升是预警这栋楼结构隐患的金丝雀。

examples.en: He kept a canary that sang every morning outside his studio.
examples.cn: 他养了一只金丝雀，每天清晨在画室外鸣唱。

examples.en: Under pressure, the suspect sang like a canary.
examples.cn: 在压力之下，嫌疑人对一切都招供了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克内瑞」——笼子可（克）内部（内）日日（瑞）有歌声，说的就是笼养的金丝雀；联想煤井里的小黄鸟一停叫大家就撤，淡黄色的小身躯格外醒目。

root: 以地名 Canary Islands（加那利群岛）命名；岛名出自拉丁语 Insulae Canariae（狗之群岛，因岛上多大型野狗），词根为拉丁语 canis（狗），可上溯至印欧词根 *ḱwṓn。因此「金丝雀」其实是「狗之鸟」，与 canine（犬的）同根。俚语「告密者」由其不停鸣唱的特征引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From the island-named songbird the word grows into an early-warning metaphor, a color name, and slang for an informer.
sensesIntro.cn: 从以岛命名的鸣禽出发，词义生长为预警的比喻、颜色名称以及指告密者的俚语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small yellow bird whose song and silence both carry messages.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只淡黄小鸟，它的歌声与沉默都传递着讯息。

branches.en: THE CAGE: the literal finch bred for color and song.
branches.cn: 鸟笼：字面义的雀鸟，为羽色与歌声而繁育。

branches.en: THE MINE: the bird that collapses first and saves the miners.
branches.cn: 矿井：先倒下却救了矿工的鸟。

branches.en: THE PAINTBOX: the yellow that borrowed the bird's name.
branches.cn: 颜料盒：借走鸟名的黄色。

branches.en: THE INTERROGATION: the singer who cannot keep quiet.
branches.cn: 审讯室：守不住嘴的歌唱者。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: both senses turn the bird's voice into information others must heed.
branches.cn: 讯息：两个义项都把鸟鸣转译成他人必须重视的信息。

intro.en: Canary is a place-name turned common noun; its derivational life sits in compounds and the dog-root family.
intro.cn: canary 是由地名转成的普通名词；其派生活动体现在复合词与「狗」词根家族中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root canis, dog, extends far beyond the bird into anatomy and everyday dog words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 canis（狗）的延伸远不止这只鸟，还进入解剖学和日常犬类词汇。

items.example: Canis familiaris, the species name of the dog

items.exampleCN: 狗之群岛（加那利群岛的拉丁名）。

items.meaning: noun-forming ending in the borrowed bird name
items.meaningCN: 借入鸟名中的名词性词尾
items.exampleCN: canary 由西班牙语 canario 转来。

items.meaning: a grass native to the Canary region
items.meaningCN: 草芦（原产加那利地区的草）

items.structure: French doublet of the same root
items.example: the dog sleeps in its kennel
He sang like a canary at the trial.
items.exampleCN: 他在庭上竹筒倒豆子般招了供。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 当心恶犬（庞贝马赛克铭文）。

definition_zh: 取消；抵消；盖销
definition_en: to decide that something planned will not happen
core_image: 在日程表上划掉一行字
scene: 雨下了一整夜，活动只能作罢。They cancelled the picnic because of the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 cancel 是「取消」（第 1 个义项：决定原定的事不再进行）；句意是因下雨他们取消了野餐。

senses.title: To call off a plan
senses.definition: to decide that a planned event will not take place
senses.definitionCN: 决定原定的活动不再举行
senses.example: They cancelled the picnic because of the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 因下雨他们取消了野餐。
senses.why: The core image is a line struck through an entry on a list.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把清单上的一行划掉。

senses.title: To balance one thing against another
senses.definition: to remove the effect of one thing by an opposite effect
senses.definitionCN: 用相反的作用去掉某事物的效果
senses.example: The two errors cancel each other out.
senses.exampleCN: 两个错误相互抵消了。
senses.why: Two marks crossing through a sum leave nothing behind.
senses.whyCN: 两笔交叉划掉一个算式，结果什么也不剩。

senses.title: To mark a ticket as used
senses.definition: to stamp a ticket or stamp so it cannot be used again
senses.definitionCN: 在票证或邮票上盖印使其不能再用
senses.example: The clerk cancelled the stamp with a date.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在邮票上盖了日期戳。
senses.why: A crossed mark showed the item had already been used.
senses.whyCN: 交叉的印记表示这件东西已经用过。

intro.en: Cancel comes from Latin words for a lattice and crossing lines.
intro.cn: cancel 来自拉丁语里表示格栅与交叉划线的词。

items.en: cancelli meant a lattice or grating.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cancelli 指格栅或栏杆。

items.en: cancellare meant to draw lines across writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cancellare 意为在文字上划交叉线。

items.en: canceler meant to cross out.
items.cn: 古法语 canceler 意为划掉。

items.en: cancellen meant to strike out writing.
items.cn: 中古英语 cancellen 意为划去文字。

items.en: Cancel covers events, offsetting effects and used tickets.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cancel 兼指取消活动、抵消作用与盖销票证。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cancel base; the near-meaning group gives other stopping verbs.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cancel 词基；近义组是其他终止类动词。

normalIntro.en: Cancel began as drawing a cross through writing.
normalIntro.cn: cancel 最初指在文字上划一个叉。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l as cancelled.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，写作 cancelled。

normal.en: Cancel out means balance completely.
normal.cn: cancel out 义为完全抵消。

normal.en: The noun is cancellation.
A cancelled flight is called off.
normal.cn: cancelled flight 指被取消的航班。

normal.en: A stamped ticket is cancelled.

abstract.en: See a pen draw two lines through a date.
abstract.cn: 想象笔在一个日期上画两道线。

abstract.en: See two arrows meet and vanish.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头相撞后消失。

abstract.en: See a round stamp press onto a corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆戳压在票角上。

examples.en: They cancelled the picnic because of the rain.
examples.cn: 因下雨他们取消了野餐。

examples.en: The two errors cancel each other out.
examples.cn: 两个错误相互抵消了。

examples.en: The clerk cancelled the stamp with a date.
examples.cn: 职员在邮票上盖了日期戳。

dict_mnemonic.text: cancel 里有 can 与 cel，像是把计划写在纸上，笔一横一竖划成格子，事情就取消了。

root: cancel 经古法语 canceler 上溯到拉丁语 cancellare，词源是 cancelli（格栅），本指在文字上划交叉线表示作废，后来泛指取消、抵消与盖销。

sensesIntro.en: Calling off a plan, balancing out an effect, and marking a ticket void.
sensesIntro.cn: 取消计划、抵消效果，以及把票证盖销作废。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines struck through a written entry.
core.cn: 核心意象：在写好的条目上划两道叉线。

intro.en: Cancel takes -ation and -ed, and combines with out.
intro.cn: cancel 能加 -ation 与 -ed，也能与 out 组合。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin cancelli, a lattice.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 cancelli，意为格栅。

definition_zh: 取消；撤销；注销；（印刷）删除线
definition_en: the act of calling off or annulling something planned or agreed; also the marking of a stamp or ticket as used
core_image: 一枚盖章作废的机票：明明印好了行程，一条红线就把它划成了废纸
scene: 台风登陆前夜，机场大厅的航班信息牌上一片红字。Passengers were told of the cancellation by text message at midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 cancellation 是「航班取消」（第 1 个义项：使既定安排作废的行为或事实）；句意是乘客们在午夜收到短信，得知航班已取消。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「取消；撤销；盖销」
动词过去分词形容词化，义为「被取消的」（美式单写 l）
同上，英式双写 l 拼法
动词加施动后缀，义为「取消者；盖销装置」

senses.title: Calling off a planned event or arrangement
senses.definition: the act or fact of deciding that a planned event, service, or trip will not happen
senses.definitionCN: 决定使原定的活动、服务或行程不再发生的行为或事实
senses.example: The cancellation of the summit disappointed reporters.
senses.exampleCN: 峰会的取消让记者们大失所望。
senses.why: The Latin cancello meant to make lattice-like crosses, the marks that void a document.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cancello 本义是打出交叉格纹，正是使文件作废的划线记号。

senses.title: Ending a contract or agreement
senses.definition: the legal termination of a contract, subscription, or standing agreement
senses.definitionCN: 对合同、订阅或长期协议的法律意义上的终止
senses.example: The cancellation clause allows either party to exit within thirty days.
senses.exampleCN: 合同中的解除条款允许任一方在三十天内退出。
senses.why: What was once crossed out by hand became, in law, a formal act of ending obligations.
senses.whyCN: 昔日手写划掉的动作，在法律中演变为正式解除义务的行为。

senses.title: Stamping or marking as used
senses.definition: the mark or process showing that a stamp or ticket has been used and cannot be used again
senses.definitionCN: 表明邮票或票据已使用、不得再次使用的记号或过程
senses.example: A crisp cancellation marked the hundred-year-old stamp.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚清晰的盖销戳标记着这枚百年邮票。
senses.why: This is the lattice mark in its original office: ink stamped across the stamp to void it.
senses.whyCN: 这正是交叉记号的原初岗位：以墨戳横盖邮票使其作废。

senses.title: Offsetting equal values
senses.definition: the elimination of equal but opposite amounts, as in accounting or algebra
senses.definitionCN: 数学或会计中相等而方向相反的量相互抵销、约去
senses.example: The cancellation of gains and losses left the ledger nearly flat.
senses.exampleCN: 盈亏相抵后，账目几乎持平。
senses.why: Two opposite strokes crossing each other leave nothing standing, so equal sums erase each other.
senses.whyCN: 两笔相交叉的笔画彼此抹去，等量的数目也就相互抵销。

intro.en: Cancellation descends from Latin cancelli, lattice bars or cross-hatching, the marks made to void a written line.
intro.cn: cancellation 源自拉丁语 cancelli（格栏、交叉线），即在文字上划出使其作废的记号。

items.en: The root *kan- relates to bending, the shape of woven lattice work.
items.cn: 词根 *kan- 与弯曲有关，正是编织格栏的形状。

items.en: Latin cancelli meant lattice, grating, or bars; the diminutive cancellus meant a small crossed line.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cancelli 指格栏、栅格；指小词 cancellus 意为一道小的交叉线。

items.en: In Roman scribal practice, to cancello a text was to cross it out with lattice strokes.
items.cn: 在罗马抄写实践中，对文本 cancello 即用交叉线将其划掉。

items.en: The verb cancel entered Middle English with the crossing-out sense, and cancellation followed for the act or the mark.
items.cn: 动词 cancel 于中古英语时期带着「划掉」义进入英语，cancellation 随之表示该行为或记号。

items.en: Modern usage centers on voided plans and agreements, with the stamp and accounting senses preserved in specialist contexts.
items.cn: 现代用法集中于被取消的计划与协议，盖销义和会计义保留在专门语境中。

note.en: Cancellation sits inside the cancel family and next to other -cel- words that confuse spelling.
note.cn: cancellation 属 cancel 词族内部，且与几个 -cel- 拼写相近的词容易混淆。

entries.definition: The base verb, to call off or cross out.
An office of a chancellor, from the lattice screens around such offices.
entries.definitionCN: 总理府、大臣官署，源自官署周围隔出格栏。

entries.definition: Spongy, lattice-like bone tissue, named for its grid structure.
entries.definitionCN: 海绵状、网格样的骨组织，因格状结构得名，同根专业词。

entries.definition: An assembly that advises; sounds partly alike but from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 议事会，发音部分相似，词根不同。

entries.definition: A formal declaration that a marriage or contract never validly existed.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告婚姻或合同自始无效的法律程序。

entries.definition: The unwinding of a contract, restoring both parties to prior positions.
entries.definitionCN: 合同的解除回转，使双方回到订约前的状态。

entries.definition: A delay rather than an ending; the event still happens later.
entries.definitionCN: 延期而非终止，活动稍后仍会举行。

entries.definition: The formal ending of a system, law, or practice.
entries.definitionCN: 对制度、法律或惯例的正式废除。

entries.definition: The restoration of something canceled to its former standing.
entries.definitionCN: 使被取消者恢复原状，是 cancellation 的反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the lattice root and the everyday cancel family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「格栏」词根与日常 cancel 词族的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root picture: Latin cancelli are lattice bars, and the cross-stroke voids a line of writing.
normal.cn: 词根画面：拉丁语 cancelli 是格栏，交叉一笔就把一行字作废。

normal.en: Spelling rule: British cancellation doubles the l after the stressed -el-; American cancels with one l.
normal.cn: 拼写规则：英式 cancellation 双写 l；美式在 canceled 中单写 l。

normal.en: Family words: cancel, cancellation, and canceler all live on the same Latin stem.
normal.cn: 词族成员：cancel、cancellation、canceler 都长在同一拉丁词干上。

normal.en: Money angle: a cancellation fee is the standard phrase for the penalty charged after backing out.
normal.cn: 金钱角度：cancellation fee 是违约取消费的标准说法。

normal.en: Same-root cousin: chancellery, a chancellor's office, keeps the lattice screen in its history.
normal.cn: 同根表亲：chancellery（总理府）在历史里保留着格栏屏风的身影。

abstract.en: A red diagonal slashed across a printed itinerary: the trip now lives only in memory.
abstract.cn: 一道红色斜线划过打印好的行程单：旅程从此只存在于记忆里。

abstract.en: Two equal opposing arrows colliding and vanishing into nothing.
abstract.cn: 两支大小相等方向相反的箭相撞后凭空消失。

abstract.en: An ink stamp blooming across a postage stamp, declaring it spent.
abstract.cn: 一方墨戳在邮票上绽开，宣告它已被使用。

examples.en: The airline offered vouchers as compensation for the cancellation.
examples.cn: 航空公司提供了代金券作为航班取消的补偿。

examples.en: Repeated cancellations of the committee meetings stalled the reform.
examples.cn: 委员会会议一再取消，改革因此停滞。

examples.en: The accountant checked the ledger for the cancellation of the duplicate entries.
examples.cn: 会计核对了账簿中重复条目的冲销情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「堪守雷申」——航班一取消，只能堪堪守在机场，雷霆大雨里申诉赔偿；联想机票被红笔划出一道道格子线，行程作废，即为取消。

root: 源自拉丁语 cancelli（格栏、栅格），指小形式 cancellus 意为小交叉线；罗马书吏以交叉线划掉文字，故 cancellare 意为「划掉、使作废」。动词经中古英语 cancel 进入英语，cancellation 由其加 -ation 构成，指取消的行为、事实或盖销记号。同根词 chancellery（官署）亦出自格栏意象。

sensesIntro.en: From the crossed-out line the word covers voided plans, terminated contracts, stamped-out tickets, and offsetting sums.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「被划掉的一行字」出发，词义涵盖被取消的计划、被解除的合同、被盖销的票证以及相互抵销的数目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cross-hatched strokes drawn over writing to void it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在文字上画出的交叉格纹，使其一笔作废。

branches.en: THE BOARD: announced events that will no longer happen.
branches.cn: 公告牌：不再举行的活动安排。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE: legal endings written into agreements.
branches.cn: 条款：写进协议的法律终止机制。

branches.en: THE POST OFFICE: ink marks that spend a stamp forever.

items.cn: 西班牙语保留了这个加勒比词。

items.en: English canoe names a dugout.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语指整木挖成的舟。

items.en: Canoeing becomes a recreation and a sport.
items.cn: 十九世纪划舟成为休闲与运动。

items.en: Canoeing enters the Olympic programme.
items.cn: 一九三六年皮划艇进入奥运项目。

items.en: Canoe covers wood, canvas and plastic hulls.
items.cn: 现代涵盖木、帆布与塑料船体。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the can- opening; the near-meaning group ranks small boats from a double-bladed kayak to a flat punt.
note.cn: 形近组共享 can- 开头；近义组把轻舟从双桨皮划艇排到平底撑船。

entries.definition: Someone who paddles a canoe.
A rule or an accepted list.
A deep narrow valley.
A narrow boat paddled from a sitting position.
A small boat moved with oars.
A flat boat of tied logs or tubes.
A flat boat moved by pushing a pole.

normalIntro.en: A canoe is a hollowed log that learned to travel.
normalIntro.cn: canoe 是一根学会旅行的挖空木头。

normal.en: Canoa was a dugout in the Caribbean.
normal.cn: canoa 是加勒比语的独木舟。

normal.en: Spanish sailors brought the word home.
normal.cn: 西班牙水手把词带回去。

normal.en: A canoe is narrow and pointed.
You move it with a paddle.
The verb is the same word.

abstract.en: A shaving of wood on still water.
abstract.cn: 静水上的一片木屑。

abstract.en: A body and a boat sharing one rhythm.
abstract.cn: 身体与船共用一种节奏。

abstract.en: Water travelled by sitting low.
abstract.cn: 坐得很低才走得动的水路。

examples.en: They paddled the canoe along the shore.
examples.cn: 他们沿岸划着独木舟。

examples.en: The canoe tipped and filled with water.
examples.cn: 独木舟翻了，灌满了水。

examples.en: We canoed to the island at sunrise.
examples.cn: 日出时我们划船去了岛上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可努」——努力划，才划得动这叶窄舟。

root: 加勒比语 canoa（独木舟）→ 西班牙语 canoa → 英语 canoe

sensesIntro.en: The boat and the journey are the same word because the boat is defined by how it moves.
sensesIntro.cn: 船与行程同词，因为这条船正是由它的行进方式定义的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow pointed hull slipping past reeds
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着一排芦苇滑过去的尖头窄船

branches.en: A hull carried down to the shore.
A race over a still lake.

branches.cn: 顺着河慢慢下去的一程。

branches.en: A boat known by its motion.

intro.en: Canoe is a Caribbean loanword; the list below adds the vocabulary of paddling, boats and navigation.
intro.cn: canoe 是加勒比借词；下面列出「划桨、船、航行」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin navis is a ship, remus is an oar, and portare is to carry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 navis 意为船，remus 意为桨，portare 意为搬运。

latinEntries.exampleCN: navis 产生 navy 与 navigate。
remus 产生 oar 与 trireme。
portare 产生 portable 与 transport。

definition_zh: 康塔塔；大合唱（声乐套曲）
definition_en: a musical composition for voices and instruments in several movements, usually on a sacred or dramatic text
core_image: 唱出来的 Sonata：歌手站成一排，管风琴托底，一乐章接一乐章地唱完一个故事
scene: 教堂晨光斜照进彩窗，唱诗班在管风琴前整队。The choir rehearsed Bach's Easter cantata for the holiday service.
sceneCN: 这里 cantata 是「康塔塔」（第 1 个义项：多乐章声乐套曲）；句意是唱诗班为节日礼拜排练巴赫的复活节康塔塔。

pos.zh: 康塔塔（多乐章声乐套曲）

collocations.phrase: a cantata for soloists and chorus
collocations.zh: 为独唱与合唱而作的康塔塔

derivatives.zh: 复合形容词，义为「康塔塔风格的」
同根音乐术语，义为「如歌的」（意大利语 cantare 同根）
对偶借词，义为「奏鸣曲」（同一构词模式，乐器版）

senses.title: A multi-movement vocal work with instruments
senses.definition: a composition for one or more voices with instrumental accompaniment, in several movements, often on a religious text
senses.definitionCN: 为独唱或合唱配器乐伴奏、分多个乐章的作品，常取宗教题材
senses.example: The church cantata alternates arias with choruses.
senses.exampleCN: 这首教堂康塔塔在咏叹调与合唱之间交替。
senses.why: The Italian name means sung piece, the voice-side twin of the played sonata.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语原名意为「唱的作品」，是「奏的」奏鸣曲在声乐一侧的孪生词。

senses.title: A large-scale choral composition generally
senses.definition: in loose modern use, any substantial work for chorus, soloists, and orchestra
senses.definitionCN: 现代宽泛用法中，泛指为合唱、独唱与乐队而作的大型作品
senses.example: The festival commissioned a cantata honoring the city's founders.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节委约了一部致敬城市奠基者的康塔塔。
senses.why: Once a genre name, it broadens to cover the family of sung multi-part works.
senses.whyCN: 它本是体裁名，随后扩展覆盖「多乐章声乐作品」这一整个家族。

intro.en: Cantata is the Italian feminine past participle of cantare, to sing, coined in the seventeenth century as the sung counterpart of the sonata, the played piece.
intro.cn: cantata 是意大利语 cantare（歌唱）的阴性过去分词，十七世纪被造出，作为「演奏的」sonata 在声乐一方的对应词。

items.en: The root *kan- means to sing or chant, ancient and widespread across Indo-European.
items.cn: 词根 *kan- 意为歌唱、吟诵，古老且遍布印欧诸语。

items.en: Latin cantare is the frequentative of canere, to sing, giving chant, cantor, and incantation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cantare 是 canere（歌唱）的反复动词形式，衍生出 chant、cantor、incantation。

items.en: Italian composers coined cantata da cantarsi, a piece to be sung, against sonata, a piece to be sounded.
items.cn: 意大利作曲家造出 cantata da cantarsi（供演唱之作），与 sonata（供演奏之作）相对。

items.en: English borrowed the term in the early eighteenth century as Italian church music spread north.
items.cn: 十八世纪初，随着意大利宗教音乐北传，英语借入了这一术语。

items.en: Today it names both the Baroque church genre and modern festival choral commissions.
items.cn: 如今它既指巴洛克教堂体裁，也指现代音乐节的委约合唱作品。

note.en: Cantata belongs to the singing family of cant- words and to the sonata pairing.
note.cn: cantata 属于 cant-「歌唱」词族，并与 sonata 构成一对。

entries.definition: A multi-movement work for instruments, the played twin of the sung cantata.
entries.definitionCN: 多乐章器乐作品，是「唱的」康塔塔的「奏的」孪生词。

entries.definition: In a singing style, a direction for instrumental players.
entries.definitionCN: 如歌地，给器乐演奏者的表情术语，同根。

entries.definition: The leader of congregational singing, especially in synagogues and churches.
entries.definitionCN: 领唱者，尤指犹太会堂或教堂中的领唱。

entries.definition: Chanted words believed to have magical power.
A large sacred choral drama, longer and more theatrical than a cantata.
entries.definitionCN: 大型宗教合唱剧，篇幅与戏剧性超过康塔塔。

entries.definition: A Lutheran hymn tune, the building block of many cantatas.
entries.definitionCN: 路德宗众赞歌，许多康塔塔的素材来源。

entries.definition: A polyphonic choral work, usually unaccompanied.
entries.definitionCN: 复调合唱作品，通常无伴奏。

entries.definition: A solo song within an opera or cantata.
entries.definitionCN: 咏叹调，歌剧或康塔塔中的独唱段落。

entries.definition: The purely instrumental large form, no singing required.
entries.definitionCN: 纯器乐的大型体裁，无需人声，与 cantata 形成对照。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the sing root and the sonata pairing.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「歌唱」词根与 sonata 配对关系的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root core: Italian cantata means a piece that is sung, from cantare.
normal.cn: 词根核心：意大利语 cantata 意为「唱出来的作品」，出自 cantare。

normal.en: Twin pair: sonata sounds, cantata sings; one letter separates the pair.
normal.cn: 孪生配对：sonata 奏、cantata 唱，两个词只差一个字母。

normal.en: Genre ladder: aria inside cantata inside oratorio, pieces nesting by size.
normal.cn: 体裁阶梯：aria 在 cantata 之内，cantata 在 oratorio 之内，按规模层层嵌套。

normal.en: Composer hook: Bach wrote over two hundred church cantatas for the Leipzig calendar.
normal.cn: 作曲家钩子：巴赫为莱比锡的礼拜年历写了二百多首教堂康塔塔。

normal.en: Family chorus: chant, cantor, cantabile, incantation all live on cant-.
normal.cn: 家族合唱：chant、cantor、cantabile、incantation 都住在 cant- 词根上。

abstract.en: Voices and organ braided together, one movement handing the story to the next.
abstract.cn: 人声与管风琴交织，一个乐章把故事递给下一个乐章。

abstract.en: A hall where the score itself seems to breathe, inhaling at the arias and exhaling in chorus.
abstract.cn: 一座乐谱仿佛在呼吸的音乐厅：咏叹调吸气，合唱吐气。

abstract.en: Two doors in one corridor: this side sings, that side plays.
abstract.cn: 同一条走廊上的两扇门：这边唱，那边奏。

examples.en: The high school choir performed a spring cantata for the town.
examples.cn: 高中合唱团为全镇演出了一部春季康塔塔。

examples.en: Scholars catalogued the cantatas by liturgical calendar.
examples.cn: 学者们按礼拜年历为这些康塔塔编目。

examples.en: Her aria floated above the orchestra in the cantata's second movement.
examples.cn: 康塔塔第二乐章里，她的咏叹调在乐队之上飘浮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坎塔塔」——站在坎（坎）台上又唱「塔塔」两声，台上人声一波接一波，正是多乐章的大合唱康塔塔；联想 sonata 是奏鸣曲，cantata 就是「唱鸣曲」。

root: 源自意大利语 cantata（cantare「歌唱」的阴性过去分词），可上溯至拉丁语 cantare（canere 的反复体），一般认为出自印欧词根 *kan-（歌唱）。十七世纪意大利作曲家以 cantata（唱的作品）与 sonata（奏的作品）相对；英语于十八世纪初借入。同根词有 chant、cantor、cantabile、incantation。

sensesIntro.en: From the Baroque sung piece the name widens to any substantial multi-part choral work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从巴洛克的声乐套曲出发，这一名称扩展为泛指一切大型多声部合唱作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: voices in movements, a story sung from first aria to final chorus.
core.cn: 核心意象：分乐章的人声，一个从首段咏叹调唱到终曲合唱的故事。

branches.en: THE LOFT: the Baroque church cantata over the congregation.
branches.cn: 唱诗楼：高悬于会众之上的巴洛克教堂康塔塔。

branches.en: THE PODIUM: modern choral commissions on secular themes.
branches.cn: 指挥台：世俗题材的现代委约合唱作品。

branches.en: THE ARCHITECTURE: arias, recitatives, and choruses stacked like floors.
branches.cn: 建筑结构：咏叹调、宣叙调与合唱如楼层般堆叠。

branches.en: THE PAIRING: sonata plays what cantata sings.
branches.cn: 配对关系：sonata 所奏即 cantata 所唱。

branches.en: THE OCCASION: civic and seasonal ceremonies borrowing the sacred form.
branches.cn: 场合：市民与节庆仪式借用这一宗教形式。

intro.en: Cantata is the Italian past participle of cantare, sung, one half of the sing-play naming pair.
intro.cn: cantata 是意大利语 cantare 的过去分词「被唱的」，是「唱-奏」命名配对的一半。

latinIntro.en: The cantare root of repeated singing feeds a wide sacred and musical family.
latinIntro.cn: cantare（反复歌唱）词根滋养出一个庞大的宗教与音乐词族。

在民众面前歌唱（拉丁语用例示意）。

items.meaningCN: 被完成的（意大利语分词词尾）

items.exampleCN: 以如歌的方式奏出旋律。
